full_judgment: 2. In the leave petition the appellant alleged that he instituted Title Suit No. 214 of 1977 (re-numbered as Title Suit No. 415 of 1984) in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet for specific performance of contract against Habiba Banu (since deceased) and respondent Nos. 1-6 as defendants on the allegations inter alia that the defendants entered into a contract with the appellant on 21-4-76 for sale of 1.09 acre of land for a consideration of Taka 2,75,143.00 by executing a bainapatra on that date and receiving Taka 50,000.00 as advance. The agreement was that the vendors would execute and register deeds of sale on receipt of the balance of consideration money by different deeds either in favour of the appellant or in favour of his nominees who are respondent Nos.7-19 in this appeal. The appellant and respondent Nos. 7-19 obtained possession of the land under contract and after dividing the said land amicably amongst themselves the appellant kept for himself three plots measuring about 39 decimals and a common pathway of about 0.06 acres of land described in Schedule-IV of the plaint which is the suit land. Respondent Nos. 1-6 and Habiba Banu executed and registered 10 different kabalas in respect of 0.64 acres of land in favour of the nominees of the appellant on receipt of Taka 2,74,500.00 out of Taka 2,75,143.00 and only Taka 643.00 remained the balance to be paid to the vendors. When the appellant demanded execution and registration of a Kabala in his favour in respect of the remaining 0.45 acres of land deceased Habiba Banu demanded Taka 50,000.(X) more on the plea of increase in the value of land. After tiling the suit the appellant obtained an order of injunction against defendant Nos. 1-7 restraining them from interfering with the possession of the appellant in the suit land.
